VERIFICATION_STATUS: DRAFT — section numbers written from working knowledge. Every rule MUST be checked against ecfr.gov before it appears on screen in the demo. A wrong citation is worse than no citation.

global_tests.test: Reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, conforms to limitations, adequately documented. A cost failing ANY of these is not allowable regardless of category.
Reasonableness — would a prudent person under the circumstances incur this?
Allocability — cost benefits the award in proportion to the benefit received. Costs benefiting more than one objective must be allocated, not assigned whole.

rules.title: Alcoholic beverages
rules.note: Unallowable outright. If bundled in a catering invoice, split the alcohol amount out and re-evaluate the remainder on its own merits under 200.432/200.438.

rules.title: Entertainment costs
rules.note: Amusement, diversion and social activities are unallowable UNLESS they have a programmatic purpose and are authorized in the approved budget or with prior written approval.

rules.title: Conferences
rules.note: Allowable where the primary purpose is dissemination of technical information and costs are necessary and reasonable. Meals at a conference are allowable; entertainment and alcohol within it are not.

rules.title: Travel costs
rules.note: Allowable if reasonable and consistent with the recipient's written travel policy. Air travel above the lowest reasonably available fare is unallowable absent documented justification (200.474(b)). Requires documented business purpose.

rules.title: Fines, penalties, damages and other settlements
Lobbying
rules.note: Costs of influencing legislation or elections are unallowable. Distinguish from allowable technical assistance provided at the request of a legislative body.

rules.title: Goods or services for personal use
Contributions and donations
rules.note: Contributions or donations MADE by the recipient are unallowable as a charge to the award.

rules.title: Advertising and public relations
rules.note: Allowable only for specified purposes — recruitment of personnel, procurement of goods, disposal of surplus, program outreach required by the award. General institutional promotion and goodwill advertising are unallowable.

rules.title: Equipment and other capital expenditures
rules.note: Capital expenditures for general purpose equipment, buildings and land are unallowable as direct charges except with prior written approval of the Federal awarding agency. Check the org capitalization threshold against 200.1 'equipment'.

rules.title: Compensation — personal services
rules.note: Allowable to the extent reasonable, but charges must be supported by records that accurately reflect the work performed. Effort/time distribution records are the evidence. No records -> missing_documentation, not unallowable.

rules.title: Allocable costs — shared benefit
rules.note: Fires when a cost plainly benefits more than one program or the organization as a whole. Do not assign the full amount to the award.

rules.title: Indirect (F&A) costs
rules.note: Recipients without a negotiated rate may elect the de minimis rate. CONFIRM THE CURRENT DE MINIMIS PERCENTAGE AND BASE AGAINST eCFR — it was revised in the 2024 OMB update. Do not hardcode from memory.

rules.title: Materials and supplies
rules.note: Allowable when necessary to carry out the award; charge at actual cost net of credits.

rules.title: Memberships, subscriptions, professional activity
rules.note: Business/technical/professional organization memberships allowable. Memberships in organizations whose primary purpose is lobbying are unallowable. Civic and community organization memberships require prior approval.

rules.title: Participant support costs
rules.note: Allowable with prior approval; moving funds OUT of this category generally requires prior approval under 200.308.

rules.title: Pre-award costs
rules.note: Allowable only to the extent they would have been allowable if incurred after the award date, and only with written approval. Fires when txn.date < period_of_performance.start.

rules.title: Revision of budget and program plans
rules.note: Fires when cumulative spend in a cost category exceeds the approved budget line beyond the agency's allowed variance. This rule is what makes the budget a live contract rather than a spreadsheet.

rules.title: Retention of records
rules.note: Supporting documentation must exist and be retained. Fires when a transaction has no attachment.

monitoring_consequences.correct_framing: A finding or a late report does not automatically make a recipient 'high-risk'. The awarding agency MAY impose specific conditions, which can include additional monitoring, additional or more frequent reporting, prior approval requirements, reimbursement-only payment, or withholding authority to proceed.
never_say: one late SF-425 makes you high-risk
